narrative.overview:
Girovo is a bank branch that opens for one person, on their own machine. Nothing on the walls sells anything, every figure is the bank's own, and the counter is tidy. The feel is **trustworthy, plain and precise**. Trust comes from exactness and calm, not from ornament. Where money could go wrong, the branch is careful first: at a risk decision the safe answer is the filled button, every layer opens on a harmless place, and every outcome is named with the same few words.

The branch is furnished in **Material 3 Expressive**, on every platform: the desktop app, the website and the Android app are one page in one look, `<html data-look="material">` (`app/layout.tsx`). `app/material.css` holds the look; `app/android.css` adds only what a phone needs. The colour is Girovo's own blue Material scheme (SchemeVibrant from the seed #0864ad), set at zero specificity so an Android phone's Material You colours can take its place. The page is flat and list-first: sections stand on the page, held apart by space, and the one container on a page is the balance. The shell is an app's, not a web page's: one top app bar that names the page, a navigation bar on phones and a navigation rail from 640px, and Überweisen as the floating action button.

Google Sans Flex sets everything, on screen and on paper, and amounts use tabular lining figures, so a column of bookings lines up on its decimal comma like a printed Kontoauszug. Colour is rationed: the scheme's primary is the one thing you can press, and green, red, amber and orange each own exactly one meaning that no wallpaper can change. The system borrows a language, never a bank's branding: the connected bank's logo appears only where the bank is the subject (the bank picker, the accounts of several banks, the Sitzung panel, the printed letterhead), never as the app's identity. The protocol stays out of the interface: FinTS segment codes and the structured tags inside a Verwendungszweck never reach the screen.
keyCharacteristics: One top app bar (title large, the page's name) over a flat page; navigation bar below 640px, navigation rail (96dp, M3 Expressive's collapsed rail) from 640px, Überweisen as the FAB.
Flat and list-first: sections stand on the page with no surface, shadow or hairline; the balance hero (28px corners, primary container) is the one container.
Girovo's fixed blue Material scheme by default, Material You on an Android phone; value colours never follow either.
Round buttons that squeeze towards square while pressed, spring motion, Material's corner scale.
Tabular figures and a real minus on every amount. Monospace only for what is read character by character.
The safe choice is the filled primary, and a dialog's buttons never scroll away.
The app's own mark is the navy "G€" plate, a logo in a fixed colour whatever the scheme.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The scheme's primary marks what can be pressed, and nothing that can be pressed is a value colour (a destructive confirm the user asked for excepted, which is Soll Red). Inside the balance hero the hero's ink stands in for it, because primary on primary-container would not read.

rules.name: The Owned Colours Rule
rules.body: Green is a credit or a confirmation. Red is a negative balance or an error, never a debit: a debit is ordinary spending and stays ink. A credit card's balance is negative by nature, so it stays ink too; a card is known by its FinTS Kontoart alone (`isCardAccount`: CreditCardAccount or 50–59), never by a product name like "Giro mit Visa", and its Verfügbar still turns red below zero. Amber means "vorgemerkt" and nothing else, so a warning uses the inset with an orange glyph instead. Orange is a mark, never text.

rules.name: The Fixed Values Rule
rules.body: Credit Green, Soll Red, Vorgemerkt Amber, Info Cyan, Marker Orange and the chart slots never take a wallpaper colour, and neither does the brand plate. Only surfaces, ink, lines and the one interactive colour follow Material You.

rules.name: The Reporting Ink Rule
rules.body: What only reports (the transfer stepper, the session countdown, budget bars, a wait spinner outside a button, the account-type plate off its row) is drawn in `headline`, which is the ink. Material's own progress indicators (the wavy bar, the loading indicator) take the primary, as Material draws them.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's default palette is switched off (`--color-*: initial`), so `red-500` does not even compile. Every colour is a token. Literal white and black exist only for literal things: the brand plate, a QR code or TAN graphic plate, the chipTAN flicker field.

rules.name: The Kontoauszug Column Rule
rules.body: Every amount goes through `<Money>`. It uses tabular lining figures and a real minus (U+2212), never a hyphen, so a column of bookings lines up on its decimal comma. Dates, counts and countdowns take `.tnum` too.

rules.name: The Weight Rule
rules.body: 400 and 500 for Material's titles, buttons and labels; 600 for a row's name and its amount and for labels above a value; 700 only for figures and for the titles of sheets and of sections off the page. Google Sans Flex at 700 thickens into a slab at 13–15px.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case and never set in capitals, on screen and on paper. A label's job is to be found, not to shout.

rules.name: The Character-by-Character Rule
rules.body: IBAN, BIC, BLZ and references are set in IBM Plex Mono. An IBAN gets 0.06em tracking and never wraps, because half an IBAN on each of two lines cannot be checked. A BLZ is grouped the way bank documents print it ("570 699 99") wherever it appears.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: No HTML text is smaller than 12px, and only Material's 12px roles (navigation labels, supporting text) and badges go below 12.5px. Monogram initials scale to their avatar, and the labels charts draw in SVG may be 11.5–12px.

rules.name: The Reading Order Rule
rules.body: The DOM order is the narrow reading order. A wider layout places blocks with the grid; it never reorders them with CSS `order`.

rules.name: The Shared Edge Rule
rules.body: The top app bar's content and the page column share one 1280px column and one gutter (`MASTHEAD_EDGES`, corrected for the scrollbar's width), so the page title and the first section align. The bar's right edge gives way to the caption buttons when they need the room.

rules.name: The Phone's Page Rule
rules.body: Below `desk` the Übersicht is the phone's: accounts, the balance, Vorgemerkt and the bookings. Summaries that would push the bookings away appear only in the side pane of a wide window.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: A block on the page is a `.panel` section: no surface, no corners, no shadow, no hairline between its rows; sections are held apart by space. The balance hero is the one container. Never put a card on the page to group a section.

rules.name: The Tonal Lift Rule
rules.body: A container is told from the page by tone, not by an edge or a shadow: the filled card, the hero, wells, the navigation bar. Shadow is for layers that float (menus, sheets, drawers, snackbars, the FAB).

rules.name: The Scroll Edge Rule
rules.body: A pinned header or footer inside a sheet is flat while everything fits. A 1px `line` hairline appears on its edge only once content runs under it, and leaves again when the content ends.

rules.name: The Safe Choice Rule
rules.body: At every risk decision the safe action is the filled primary and the risky one the tonal button beside it: "Angaben prüfen" at a duplicate or a name mismatch, "Namen übernehmen" when the bank suggests the name, "Angaben ändern" after a refusal, "Jetzt nachsehen" at Status unklar, "Umsätze prüfen" before logging out or restarting over an unclear transfer. A destructive confirmation the user asked for keeps its red confirm, with the safe button focused.

rules.name: The Safe Focus Rule
rules.body: A layer opens on the safe place: what it names (`initialFocus`, or `[data-autofocus]` on its safe button), else its first text field, else its close button, else the layer itself. Never a checkbox, switch, radio, link or action by default. A `[data-autofocus="fine"]` field takes focus only with a fine pointer, so a touch keyboard never covers a layer as it opens.

rules.name: The Pinned Way Out Rule
rules.body: A dialog's actions and a panel's closing action sit in a footer below the scrolling body, so they never scroll away, whatever the window's height or zoom. A wait that runs against a deadline pins its status there with them.

rules.name: The Record Rule
rules.body: Paper prints the bank's words as the bank sent them, repairing only encoding damage. Where the sheet leads with a name the app derived, "Name laut Bank" prints the whole string beside it.

rules.name: The Bank's Figure Rule
rules.body: A balance is the bank's only when the bank sent it. Otherwise it is worked out and marked "(errechnet)". Future-dated bookings print apart ("Noch nicht enthalten"), and a gap the bookings cannot explain is printed with its size, never adjusted to fit.

rules.name: The Same State Rule
rules.body: Paper states a booking's state the way the screen does (gebucht, vorgemerkt, noch nicht gebucht), and an unbooked state gets a sentence under the amount, not only a word.

rules.name: The Third-Party Rule
rules.body: Paper speaks in the third person and carries only what its reader needs. The Buchungsbeleg shows the booking, never the account's balance, a merchant logo, a note or a receipt; a Mitteilung shows the message, never an account or the login name.

rules.name: The Two-Sign Rule
rules.body: On paper a debit is ink and a credit green, and both signs (+ and −) are written out, so a grey copy says the same. A balance carries only its minus.

rules.name: The Summenstrich Rule
rules.body: The final balance sits between a 1px rule and a 3px double rule. No box.

rules.name: The Fileable Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing on paper is smaller than 8pt, mono included, and running text is 9.5pt. The 20mm left margin lets a punched, filed sheet keep every character, and every printed page carries the document, the account and "Seite x von y" in its bottom margin.

dos: Do reach for tokens by name (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-2`, `bg-accent`, `var(--nav-bg)`), never a `--md-*` role straight in a component unless Material names that role for it (the search pill's container colours). The theme and Material You then resolve themselves.
Do put the look in `app/material.css` for every platform, and only phone behaviour (status bar, touch targets, sheets, type scale, ripple) in `app/android.css` behind `data-platform="android"`.
Do keep Girovo's scheme at zero specificity (`:where(:root[data-look='material'])`), so Material You's runtime roles always win on the phone.
Do build a page block as a `.panel` section on the page and let space separate sections; the balance hero is the only container in `#main`.

Do route every amount through `<Money>` (tabular figures, U+2212 minus, role-based colour, privacy mask), bank free text through `<BankText>`, and every IBAN through the `.iban` mono style, which never wraps.
Do decide whether a balance is a card's with `isCardAccount` (the Kontoart), and pass `tone="plain"` for it.
Do give primitives their data hooks (`data-size`, `data-variant`, `data-segmented`, `data-field`, `data-dialog`, `data-chip`, `data-icon-button`) so the Material rules reach them.
Do use the floating-label `Field` for a field whose label stands alone on its row.
Do make the safe answer the filled primary at every risk decision, with the risky action as the tonal button beside it.
Do give a dialog or panel its actions as a pinned `footer`, so they stay in view in a 900×600 window and at 200%.
Do let layers open on the safe place (safeFocusTarget).
Do name every outcome with the shared words: Freigabe, Abruf fehlgeschlagen, unvollständig, nicht ausgeführt, Status unklar.
Do give every icon-only control an `aria-label`. It doubles as its tooltip.
Do animate with the M3E springs: spatial for position, size and shape, effects for colour and opacity. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep the desktop shell's `BAR_COLORS` equal to `bar` and `bar-ink` in both themes.
Do write the markup in the narrow reading order and place blocks with the grid on wider screens.
Do give charts colours by rank (top six, rest grey), Credit Green for income and navy-slate for spending.
Do use the spaced Gedankenstrich (" – ") in interface strings, and German quotes („…“).
donts: Don't colour a debit red, or a credit card's balance. Spending is not an error, and a card is negative by nature.
Don't let a value colour, a chart slot or the brand plate follow Material You.
Don't use amber for a warning. Amber means "vorgemerkt"; a warning is the inset plus an orange glyph.
Don't set orange as text. It is a dot, an edge, a ring or a glyph.
Don't put a card, a shadow or a hairline grid on the page to group a section, or frame a card inside a card.
Don't bring back an outlined secondary button; the second emphasis is the tonal button.
Don't set labels in capitals or letterspace them beyond Material's own tracking, on screen or on paper.
Don't use Tailwind's default palette (`red-500`, `slate-200`). It is switched off on purpose.
Don't show FinTS segment codes or a Verwendungszweck's structured tags in the interface, or print them on paper.
Don't put the risky action in the filled button at a risk decision, or open a layer on a checkbox, a switch, a radio or an action.
Don't let a dialog's buttons scroll away with its text.
Don't fill a chart area with a gradient. The Kontoverlauf area is flat.
Don't let a theme or the screen's scheme reach paper. The `.doc` tokens are fixed light values.
Don't colour the chipTAN flicker field or the TAN scan plate with the theme; the generator reads contrast.
Don't use any bank's logo, wordmark or name as the app's own identity.
